\[
\boxed{\sqrt{\frac{29+4\sqrt7}{108}}}
\]

Let \(V=[v_1\ v_2\ v_3\ v_4]\), and let

\[
G=V^{T}V
\]

be the Gram matrix of the basis. Since \(\|v_i\|=1\), the diagonal entries of \(G\) are all \(1\). The dual basis matrix is

\[
W=V^{-T},
\]

so

\[
W^{T}W=V^{-1}V^{-T}=G^{-1}.
\]

Thus \(\|w_i\|^2=2\) says that the diagonal entries of \(G^{-1}\) are all \(2\).

We want

\[
|\det V|=\sqrt{\det G}.
\]

Let the eigenvalues of \(G\) be \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_4>0\). Then

\[
\sum_{i=1}^4 \lambda_i=\operatorname{tr}G=4,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^4 \frac1{\lambda_i}=\operatorname{tr}G^{-1}=8.
\]

So it remains to maximize

\[
P=\lambda_1\lambda_2\lambda_3\lambda_4
\]

under these two constraints.

At an interior maximum, Lagrange multipliers give

\[
\frac1{\lambda_i}=\alpha-\frac{\beta}{\lambda_i^2},
\]

so every \(\lambda_i\) is a root of the same quadratic. Hence the eigenvalues take at most two distinct values.

If the multiplicities are \(2,2\), say \(a,a,b,b\), then

\[
a+b=2,\qquad \frac1a+\frac1b=4,
\]

so \(ab=\frac12\), giving

\[
P=(ab)^2=\frac14.
\]

If the multiplicities are \(1,3\), say \(a,b,b,b\), then

\[
a+3b=4,\qquad \frac1a+\frac3b=8.
\]

Substituting \(a=4-3b\) gives

\[
6b^2-10b+3=0,
\]

so

\[
b=\frac{5\pm\sqrt7}{6}.
\]

The product is

\[
P=ab^3=(4-3b)b^3=\frac{8b+3}{36},
\]

hence the larger value is

\[
P_{\max}=\frac{29+4\sqrt7}{108}.
\]

This exceeds \(\frac14\), so it is the maximal possible determinant of \(G\).

It remains to show this value is attainable. Let

\[
a=\frac{3-\sqrt7}{2},\qquad b=\frac{5+\sqrt7}{6},
\]

and let \(P_0\) be the rank-one orthogonal projection onto the span of

\[
u=\frac12(1,1,1,1).
\]

Define

\[
G=bI+(a-b)P_0.
\]

Then \(G\) has eigenvalues \(a,b,b,b\), so

\[
\det G=ab^3=\frac{29+4\sqrt7}{108}.
\]

Also each diagonal entry of \(P_0\) is \(1/4\), so each diagonal entry of \(G\) is

\[
\frac{a+3b}{4}=1,
\]

and each diagonal entry of \(G^{-1}\) is

\[
\frac{1/a+3/b}{4}=2.
\]

Thus such a Gram matrix is feasible, and therefore

\[
\max |\det V|
=
\sqrt{\det G}
=
\boxed{\sqrt{\frac{29+4\sqrt7}{108}}}.
\]
